item.text:
**Verdict:** mixed, leaning no. Sharif made some plainly true, low-drama public statements on diplomacy and security, but the 2024 record also shows repeated information control, media pressure, and judicial/political intimidation. I did not find a single definitive 2024 transcript proving a major lie in parliament or court; the case against him is cumulative and indirect, but substantial.

**Accepted Claims**
- **UNGA push for Kashmir dialogue** | **Radio Pakistan** | **2024-09-27** | [URL](https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute) | Sharif publicly urged India to negotiate a peaceful Kashmir settlement. This is a straightforward statement that matches a de-escalatory posture rather than a deceptive one. | `7B.1`
- **UK arms-control dialogue** | **Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan** | **2024-05-16** | [URL](https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/6th-round-of-pakistan-uk-dialogue-on-arms-control-non-proliferation) | Pakistan held a formal arms-control and nonproliferation dialogue with the UK and pledged continued coordination in multilateral fora. This is evidence of at least some honest engagement with an international partner. | `7B.1`
- **Counterterrorism campaign with provincial consensus** | **Radio Pakistan** | **2024-06-22** | [URL](https://www.radio.gov.pk/22-06-2024/pm-for-collective-efforts-to-eliminate-menace-of-terrorism) | Sharif announced a national counterterrorism campaign backed by provincial consensus and resources. The statement is tied to visible security activity, not obviously to a false public narrative. | `7B.1`
- **Peaceful, defensive nuclear messaging** | **Radio Pakistan** | **2024-12-24** | [URL](https://www.radio.gov.pk/24-12-2024/pm-vows-to-root-out-scourge-of-terrorism) | Sharif said Pakistan’s nuclear program was for self-defense and had no aggressive designs. That is restrained public messaging, even if it is also reputationally useful. | `7B.1`
- **X block justified as national security** | **Reuters via Investing.com** | **2024-04-17** | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313) | The government acknowledged blocking X on national-security grounds. Rights groups and civil society treated the restriction as harmful to monitoring and accountability, so this reads as a self-serving justification for information control. | `7B.1`
- **Media pressure and predetermined narrative** | **U.S. Department of State** | **2024** | [URL](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128431.html) | The report says journalists faced pressure to follow a predetermined narrative, and that PEMRA, PTA, network access, advertising, and FIA notices were used to suppress threatening information. This is strong evidence against habitual truth-telling to the public and media. | `7B.1`
- **Clampdown on dissenting media and NGOs** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-01-11** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent) | HRW said the government clamped down on dissenting media, the opposition, and NGOs, deepening self-censorship. A ruler who relies on this kind of environment is not operating in a truth-forward way. | `7B.1`
- **Judicial independence weakened by the 26th Amendment** | **The Guardian** | **2024-10-21** | [URL](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps) | Critics said the amendment weakened judicial independence and passed amid allegations of intimidation and abductions of MPs. That undercuts truthful dealing with courts and suggests a preference for power over candor. | `7B.1`
- **PTI crackdown with arrests and internet cuts** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-10-09** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent) | HRW reported mass arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, and mobile-internet cuts against peaceful protesters. That is consistent with a government that suppresses scrutiny rather than tells the full truth when it is costly. | `7B.1`
- **Baloch protest repression** | **Amnesty International** | **2024-07-30** | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/pakistan-repeated-punitive-crackdowns-on-baloch-protests-must-end/) | Amnesty described deaths, mass arrests, roadblocks, and network shutdowns against Baloch protesters. This is further evidence that the state preferred control and narrative management over open truthfulness under pressure. | `7B.1`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find a clean 2024 document showing Sharif himself making a directly provable false statement in parliament, court, or a bilateral meeting.
- The strongest negative evidence is structural: censorship, platform blocks, media pressure, and coercive handling of dissent.
- So the best answer is not “proven liar in every setting,” but “not reliably truth-forward when truth threatened power, reputation, or control.”
